title: A method for the characterisation of microplastics in sludge
author: Campo, Holmes, et al.

steps.title: Collect and store sludge sample
steps.instruction: Collect 1 L wet wastewater sludge from the upper section of the sludge holding tank using a metal scoop, transfer it into a rinsed 1‑L glass bottle, and mix the bottle to keep solids suspended.

steps.title: Prepare spiked subsamples
steps.instruction: Aliquot 50 mL of the mixed sludge into glass vials, spike each in triplicate with low‑density polyethylene (LDPE) fragments of size ranges 5–1 mm, 1–0.5 mm, or 500–150 µm at either 10 or 100 fragments (corresponding to 0.01 % or 0.11 % wet weight), stir for 15 min while covered with aluminum foil, and keep each spiked subsample in triplicate for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 50 mL of mixed sludge into a glass vial.
Add LDPE fragments of the desired size range (5–1 mm, 1–0.5 mm, or 500–150 µm) at the chosen spike level (10 or 100 fragments, i.e., 0.01 % or 0.11 % wet weight).
Stir the vial for 15 min with the cap covered by aluminum foil to avoid airborne contamination.
Prepare three replicate vials for each spike condition.

steps.title: Purify LDPE fragments
steps.instruction: Freeze‑dry each supernatant and pellet fraction, place each in a 250‑mL glass beaker, add 20 mL Fenton’s reagent (0.05 M) and 20 mL H₂O₂ (30 %), heat on a magnetic stirrer to 60 °C and react for 15 min; add 10 mL H₂O₂ after 30 min and again after 90 min, then let the mixture react for a further 12 h; finally recombine LDPE fragments from both fractions by consecutively sieving the reaction mixtures.

substeps.instruction: Place each freeze‑dried fraction (supernatant or pellet) into a 250‑mL glass beaker.
Add 20 mL of Fenton’s reagent (0.05 M) and 20 mL of H₂O₂ (30 %).
Put the beaker on a magnetic stirrer, heat to 60 °C, and maintain for 15 min.
Add an additional 10 mL of H₂O₂ after 30 min of reaction.
Add another 10 mL of H₂O₂ after 90 min of reaction.
Continue the reaction for a total of 12 h.
Recombine LDPE fragments from both fractions by consecutively sieving the reaction mixtures.
